entities.summary:
The Battle of Vouille, fought on September 24, 507 CE, marked a pivotal moment in the history of Western Europe as the Frankish king Clovis I led his forces to a decisive victory over the Visigoths, led by Alaric II, in the region of Vouillé, modern-day France.

This clash of titans had profound consequences, as the Frankish expansion led to the eventual collapse of the Visigothic kingdom, paving the way for the rise of the Frankish Empire under Clovis.

The Battle of Vouille is often regarded as a turning point in the Frankish-Visigothic conflict, which had significant implications for the course of European history in the centuries to come.

The battle's legacy can be seen in the enduring cultural and political influences of the Frankish Empire, with Clovis's descendants going on to shape the course of European politics and society for centuries to come.
